claims.text: In Mondweep Chakravorty's run the vault is written or read in three steps of twelve: written in step 5, read in step 8, read and rejected in step 11.
claims.quote: The vault is written in 5, read in 8, read and rejected in 11.

value.unit: steps in which the vault is written or read

claims.text: In step 6 the vault is what the policy guards, and in step 7 it outlives the deletion of the project.
claims.quote: In 6 it is what the policy guards; in 7 it outlives the deletion.

claims.text: The vault is a recovery copy of Ruflo's memory database, sealed with fingerprints of the data, the ABP and the compiled policy.
claims.quote: A recovery copy of Ruflo's memory database, sealed with fingerprints of the data, the ABP and the compiled policy.

claims.text: It is stored in a checkpoint folder on the same machine as encrypted SGit objects, with the keys in a separate private folder.
claims.quote: A checkpoint folder on the same machine, as encrypted SGit objects, with the keys in a separate private folder.

claims.text: It is implemented inside the adapter, a local MCP server at version 0.2 calling the SGit library at a pinned commit; each checkpoint gets its own vault, and Ruflo knows nothing about it.
claims.quote: Each checkpoint gets its own SGit vault, and only its encrypted bare store leaves the adapter's private staging.

claims.text: The ABP applies to the adapter's tools in steps 4, 5, 6, 8 and 11; Ruflo's own command line, in steps 3, 9 and 10, does not pass through it.
claims.quote: Ruflo's own command line, in steps 3, 9 and 10, does not pass through it

claims.text: Of Ruflo, the memory store and retrieve commands, the SQLite file, the bundled embedding model and a pinned evaluator ran; not its hive-mind, its running policy state or vector search.
claims.quote: Not its hive-mind, not its running policy state, not vector search.

claims.text: The analysis keeps apart what is shown on screen and what is inferred, and says where Mondweep's published code settles an inference; solid arrows are on screen or confirmed, dashed ones inferred.
claims.quote: solid arrows are on screen or confirmed by the code, and dashed ones are inferred

claims.text: Two lines run from the test script: Ruflo's command line writes the memory file directly, and the adapter's tools each pass a policy gate, Ruflo's evaluator in enforce mode failing closed, before reaching the SGit library.
claims.quote: Each passes a policy gate, a pinned copy of Ruflo's evaluator running the compiled ABP rules in enforce mode, which fails closed

claims.text: In step 5 the checkpoint for the project namespace is allowed; the adapter takes a consistent copy of Ruflo's memory file with a SQLite backup, fingerprints it, and SGit stores it encrypted.
claims.quote: The adapter takes a consistent copy of Ruflo's memory file with a SQLite backup, fingerprints it, and SGit stores it encrypted

claims.text: The code confirms the order: a policy check, a consistent SQLite backup, an integrity check, a new SGit vault and a commit, then only the encrypted bare store copied out of staging; no remote push is performed.
claims.quote: No remote push is performed.

claims.text: The README is precise that the hashes bind evidence to a mandate and are not digital signatures or immutable audit receipts.
claims.quote: These hashes bind evidence to a mandate; they are not digital signatures or immutable audit receipts.

claims.text: The checkpoint records which policy was in force when it was taken, so a restore can be tied to the rules that governed the data; this is the part to point every architect at.
claims.quote: the checkpoint records which policy was in force when it was taken, so a restore can be tied to the rules that governed the data

claims.text: In step 8 a brand-new adapter process restores the checkpoint into fresh-runner, and the restored database is byte for byte the one saved in step 5.
claims.quote: The restored database is byte for byte the one saved in step 5.

claims.text: The code confirms the restore checks the ciphertext digest, decrypts with the private key record, checks the manifest and database digest and the SQLite file, then promotes it to a new workspace; it never overwrites an existing one.
claims.quote: It never overwrites an existing workspace.

claims.text: In step 11 one encrypted object is altered and a restore is tried; the ABP allows the restore, and the adapter's check of the stored ciphertext is what refuses it.
claims.quote: The ABP allows the restore; the adapter's check of the stored ciphertext is what refuses it.

claims.text: Before anything is decrypted the adapter compares the ciphertext digest with the one recorded and refuses with a mismatch error; SGit is never asked to decrypt the altered copy.
claims.quote: SGit is never asked to decrypt the altered copy.

claims.text: In step 6 the vault is what the policy protects and is not touched; in step 7 the vault and its keys survive the deletion because they live in folders outside the project.
claims.quote: the vault and its keys survive because they live in folders outside the project

claims.text: Encryption happens on the machine and the ciphertext stays there; the README lists remote sync as a follow-up, so the vault survives the project being deleted but would not survive the machine being lost.
claims.quote: It would not survive the machine being lost, which the video does not claim.

claims.text: The step to see next: push the same objects to a vault server that holds only ciphertext and restore on another machine, showing the server holding nothing readable.
claims.quote: A second run that restores on a different machine, and shows the server holding nothing readable, would close the loop.

claims.text: Three steps of twelve is not a weakness: a recovery copy should be touched when you save and when you restore, and otherwise left alone, or it would be working memory, not a backup.
claims.quote: A recovery copy should be touched when you save and when you restore, and otherwise left alone.

claims.text: Because the adapter wraps Ruflo's memory file from outside through MCP, the same pattern could wrap any agent tool that keeps its memory in a file, and the vault is only as complete as the adapter's reach.
claims.quote: the same adapter pattern could wrap any agent tool that keeps its memory in a file, without changing the tool

claims.text: The account is from the screen and the code; where a diagram goes beyond both, the arrow is dashed and the text says inferred.
claims.quote: Where a diagram goes beyond both, the arrow is dashed and the text says inferred.

claims.text: It is not a review of SGit's cryptography; the tampered object is caught by the adapter's digest check, before decryption.
claims.quote: Not a review of SGit's cryptography.

claims.text: It is not a criticism of the run; one machine is what a proof of concept on a laptop looks like.
claims.quote: One machine is what a proof of concept on a laptop looks like.

claims.text: Ruflo's unused parts are not judged; they were outside this test's scope.
claims.quote: They were outside this test's scope.

claims.text: The architecture is an addendum to the analysis made for the author by Claude on 17 October 2026 from on-screen content, corrected where the code shows otherwise, and checked by the site's agent.
claims.quote: an addendum to the analysis made for me by Claude (Anthropic) on 17 October 2026 from on-screen content
